brief.headline: Samsung/Hynix diverge intraday as HBM4 rotation collides with positioning unwind
brief.summary: <cite index="46-1,46-3">Samsung edged +0.8% while SK Hynix dropped ~5% on August 7, an unusual split signaling investor rotation toward diversified AI memory exposure with less single-niche risk.</cite> <cite index="45-1,45-2,45-3">Top 1% traders at Mirae Asset net-sold Hynix for a second day as the stock fell 4.48% to 1.428M won, cutting losses after Thursday's 10.37% plunge.</cite> <cite index="12-6,12-7">DDR4 prices jumped 14.3% MoM to $24 in July, while NAND rose 4.3% to $30.1, with both hitting record highs on AI-driven capacity diversion.</cite> <cite index="33-2,33-3,33-4">TSMC's CoWoS capacity is projected to reach 130-140k wafers/month by end-2026 (vs 70k in 2025), but supply-demand gap remains at ~20% despite Nvidia locking 800-850k wafers for the year.</cite>
brief.pair_trade_view: Long Samsung vs short SK Hynix on 3-6 month view. <cite index="48-1,48-4,48-5">All three suppliers passed Nvidia Vera Rubin HBM4 certification in June, with SK Hynix holding 60-70% volume allocation, Samsung 25-30%, and Samsung starting mass production in February 2026.</cite> <cite index="53-2,53-3">Samsung is set to lead Vera Rubin-specific HBM4 supply while SK Hynix takes over half of Nvidia's total HBM in 2026; Samsung's global HBM bit share climbs from 20% to 28% vs Hynix down from 59% to 50%.</cite> Samsung's diversified revenue base (memory + foundry + logic) offers downside cushion if hyperscaler capex tightens. Hynix trades at heroic multiples embedding flawless HBM execution through 2027—any demand normalization or pricing pushback torches the premium. <cite index="20-1,20-5,20-6">Microsoft raised 2026 capex $25B to $190B but attributed entire increase to component price inflation, not new capacity, signaling potential hyperscaler spending discipline ahead.</cite>

memory_cycle.notes: <cite index="11-1,15-1,15-2">TrendForce projects DRAM contract prices +13-18% QoQ in Q3 2026, NAND +10-15% QoQ—substantial but marked slowdown from Q2's 58-63% DRAM and 70-75% NAND jumps.</cite> <cite index="8-11">Bank of America forecasts global DRAM revenue +51% in 2026, NAND +45%, with ASPs climbing >30%.</cite> <cite index="8-3,8-12,8-13">Top three memory makers have pre-sold full HBM output for 2026, with Micron guiding 68% gross margin in Q2 2026.</cite> Consumer pricing resistance building: <cite index="11-4,11-5">Higher memory costs feeding into retail, expected to weigh on PC shipments; smartphone vendors raising handset prices to offset LPDRAM costs while becoming cautious with production.</cite> <cite index="9-1,9-2">Memory shortages expected to last through 2027, giving leading suppliers stronger pricing power than industry historically enjoyed.</cite>

brief.hbm_pulse: <cite index="5-6">HBM bit shipments projected to jump 35% in 2026 to 17.1B Gb.</cite> <cite index="9-3">SK Hynix controlled 57% of global HBM revenue share in Q4 2025, Samsung 22%, Micron 21%.</cite> <cite index="5-7">Hynix expects only 'minimal to modest downtick' in HBM3E pricing for 2026 vs 2025 as more suppliers come online.</cite> <cite index="8-2,8-9">HBM3E remains dominant AI memory through 2026 with pricing power intact until new capacity after 2027; SK Hynix is only supplier able to deliver both HBM3E and HBM4 at scale.</cite> Samsung qualification win changes narrative: <cite index="52-4">Samsung's HBM4 achieves 11.7 Gb/s data rate, exceeding Nvidia/AMD's 10 Gb/s requirement—highest-performing spec in industry.</cite> <cite index="56-2,56-3">Samsung passed Nvidia's 12-layer HBM3E qual in Sept 2025 (third supplier after Hynix/Micron) and reached volume shipments Oct 2025, with 2026 supply reportedly sold out; ~18-month qualification struggle spanned entire Blackwell cycle.</cite>

news_pulse.headline: Samsung/Hynix diverge for first time in AI rally as top traders rotate
news_pulse.implication: Positioning unwind favors diversified Samsung over pure-play Hynix. Validates pair trade thesis if sustained beyond today's session.

news_pulse.headline: DDR4 +14.3% MoM to $24, NAND +4.3% to $30.1 in July—19-month rally continues
news_pulse.implication: Conventional memory pricing acceleration into July supports near-term gross margin upside for both names, but consumer resistance building.

news_pulse.headline: TSMC expands CoW outsourcing to ASE/OSATs as CoWoS gap narrows to ~10% by end-2026
news_pulse.implication: Packaging bottleneck easing faster than expected—removes structural HBM delivery constraint but also reduces scarcity premium into 2H27.

news_pulse.headline: Microsoft raises 2026 capex to $190B, attributes entire $25B increase to component inflation not new capacity
news_pulse.implication: First hyperscaler signal of spending discipline. If AWS/Google follow, memory demand could decelerate faster than buyside expects.

news_pulse.headline: Q3 DRAM price growth slows to +13-18% QoQ vs Q2's +58-63%, NAND +10-15% vs +70-75%
news_pulse.implication: Memory upcycle decelerating—fits late-expansion thesis. Watch for Q4 guide cuts if consumer markets crack.

news_pulse.headline: Nvidia locked 800-850k CoWoS wafers for 2026 (>50% of TSMC total capacity), gap still 20%
news_pulse.implication: Nvidia's capacity lock extends HBM demand visibility but crowding out AMD/Broadcom/hyperscaler custom silicon could diversify supplier risk.

news_pulse.headline: Hyperscaler Q1 2026 capex hit $112B quarterly; Google Cloud +63% YoY, AWS +28%, Azure +40%
news_pulse.implication: Demand backdrop remains intact through Q1, but July Alphabet capex raise sparked 7% selloff—market tolerance for incremental spend declining.

news_pulse.headline: Samsung HBM4 mass production started Feb 2026, qualified at 11.7 Gb/s (vs 10 Gb/s Nvidia spec)
news_pulse.implication: Samsung HBM4 performance parity achieved—removes technical discount vs Hynix in Vera Rubin allocations. 2026 supply sold out per multiple sources.

brief.derivatives_signal: No KOSPI 200 futures or options data in payload. Intraday price action shows Samsung holding gains while Hynix gave back early rebound—<cite index="39-11,39-12,39-13,39-15,39-16">Samsung opened +2.49% at 9:15am, narrowed to +0.98% at 11:20am; Hynix opened higher but recovery lost momentum quickly, with Samsung's relative strength vs Hynix a notable feature of Friday trading.</cite> Foreign flow turned net seller after early bargain hunt per KRX reporting. August leveraged single-stock ETF vol remains elevated post-July circuit breaker events. Watch Samsung/Hynix pair spread: if Samsung sustains outperformance through next week, confirms rotation from pure HBM beta to diversified semis exposure.
watch_for_next_3h: KOSPI close and foreign institution net flow—confirm whether 0900 KST buying was dead-cat bounce or sustained rotation
Any Samsung/SK Hynix ADR (SSNLF/HXSCL) volume/price action in US pre-market as US funds react to divergence
Hyperscaler (MSFT/GOOGL/AMZN) commentary or leaks on Q3 capex plans—Microsoft's inflation-only guidance shift needs confirmation
TSMC/ASE/Amkor statements on CoWoS outsourcing scale and timeline—if 10% supply gap by Dec confirmed, removes 2027 bottleneck thesis faster than expected
